indicators.note: the inclusion of one piece during the other means it is placed inside the word for interval

parts.note: a rest is an interval or pause
one is I in Roman numerals, and the 's stands for 'is', giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone objects to being included in a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclusion during' puts IS (one's, read as 'one is') inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to stand against or oppose it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Old testament priest, old testament poet

parts.note: Eli was the priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A list pairing a biblical priest with a poet from the same scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition of 'old testament' suggests both halves describe biblical figures, but the second only supplies the abbreviation OT, and 'poet' is the definition: T. S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the American-born British writer of The Waste Land, a famous modern versifier.

clue.text: At home repair is wide of the mark

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to repair a fault is to correct it

explanation.surface: A domestic fix-it job goes badly astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide of the mark misses its target, so it is wrong or mistaken.

parts.note: courting suggests romance, but here it means playing on a court, and couples are doubles pairs in a racket sport

explanation.definitionFit: This racket sport is played on a court, often by pairs in a doubles match.

clue.text: Vehicle owner turned out to be haggard

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of the word owner are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist turns out to look exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' reworks OWNER into EWORN, placed after CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggard face is drawn and tired, as is one worn down by worry.

parts.note: in cricket one form of dismissal is a single event, yet its name contains two separate ways of getting a batsman out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out when the bowler catches the ball off their own bowling; the name joins two separate modes of dismissal, hence 'once or twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket dismissal happens when the bowler takes the catch from their own delivery.

clue.text: It is hard without part of the bible

parts.note: the Book of Ruth is part of the Old Testament
less can mean without, as in 'five less two'

explanation.surface: A remark that something is difficult when lacking a section of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' is a link phrase; read 'without part of the bible' as 'Ruth less'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruthless person is pitiless and hard-hearted, lacking compassion.

clue.text: Height of unnatural growth first on island

indicators.note: first says the word for unnatural growth goes before the abbreviation for height

parts.note: a wig is artificial hair, a growth that is not natural

explanation.surface: A measurement of some strange growth found on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight lies off the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wight is an island in the English Channel, off Hampshire.

clue.text: Not wearing anything smooth on one's feet

definitions.text: Not wearing anything smooth on one's feet

parts.words: Not wearing anything smooth on one's feet
parts.note: the phrase describes footwear that is rough rather than smooth, the literal origin of a phrase meaning domineering

explanation.definitionFit: Literally describing horseshoes with projecting nails for grip; figuratively, riding over others means treating them harshly.

clue.text: Leading mischief-maker is to lead the bad behaviour

indicators.note: Leading picks out the first letter of the word mischief-maker that follows it

parts.note: taken as written
to conduct an orchestra or a tour is to lead it

explanation.surface: The chief troublemaker is set to head some misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' takes M from mischief-maker; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or wrongful conduct is bad behaviour, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Leave out the absence of oxygen, creating something very painful

indicators.note: the absence of says one letter is removed from the phrase for leave out

parts.note: to go out is to leave
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Excluding oxygen produces an agonising condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the absence of' drops one O from GO OUT, leaving GOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of arthritis causes intense swelling and pain, especially in the big toe.

parts.note: brilliant suggests a gifted athlete, but it hints at something shining in the sky, and the swimmer is a sea creature

explanation.definitionFit: This sea creature typically has five radiating limbs and is named for a celestial shape.

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some fruit has split and been chipped.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee, also spelt this way, is a sweet Chinese fruit with a rough shell.

indicators.note: after says the word be follows the abbreviation for his Excellency

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instruction to follow an ambassador's servant who pours his wine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Hebe was cupbearer to the gods before Ganymede.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe, goddess of youth, served nectar to the Olympian gods.

definitions.meaning: a sally is a sudden outing or sortie
a trip is a short journey or jaunt

explanation.surface: A girl named Sally is going on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sally' as a common noun, not a name; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sortie and a jaunt are short journeys out and back.

indicators.note: spilling suggests the letters of I shan't be are tipped out and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A careful drinker vows not to spill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' rearranges ISHANTBE.
explanation.definitionFit: This green anise-flavoured spirit is a strong alcoholic liquor.

indicators.note: removed signals that the letters of tags Colin are shifted from their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has taken Colin's labels off, feeling wistful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges TAGSCOLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling wistful longing for the past is being sentimental about it.

clue.text: Damage fastener before taking an item of food

indicators.note: before taking says the fastener comes ahead of and then picks up the word an

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
a zip is a fastener on clothing

explanation.surface: A broken zip on a lunch bag.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond paste is a confection used on cakes and in sweets.

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
land is real estate, a form of property

explanation.surface: Paying duty on real estate in rural areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot' is an old tax, surviving in 'scot-free'; 'the country' points to a nation, not rural areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland is a nation in the north of Great Britain.

definitions.meaning: an edge or boundary of a shape
Leicestershire is an English county cricket club, an example of a team

explanation.surface: A cricket boundary at a Leicestershire ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicestershire is an English county with a first-class cricket team; 'boundary' hints at cricket but means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge marks a limit, and a sports team is a squad; the word covers both.

clue.text: Spaniard captured Italian leader, one of higher rank

indicators.note: captured means the Spaniard's title holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: señor is the Spanish title for a man

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of the word Italian

explanation.surface: A Spanish soldier seized an Italian commander who outranked him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' puts I (Italian's first letter) inside SENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior is someone above another in status or seniority.

clue.text: Tears round with last character as substitute

indicators.note: round signals that the letters of tears are turned about into another order

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over a stand-in being chosen last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges TEARS into ERSAT, then add Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ersatz is an inferior replacement or imitation.

indicators.note: first says the symbol for silver goes ahead of the word for base

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
base means low or mean

explanation.surface: Base metal placed above silver is gleaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing with light or colour, so brightly lit or radiant.

clue.text: Work to the right of the machinist

parts.note: an opera is a musical work (also opus)
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A task placed on the right side of a mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a machine is its user or minder.

clue.text: Proposal to get cold off one's chest

indicators.note: off says the letter for cold is taken away from the word for chest

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A suggestion to cure a chesty cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes C from COFFER; 'get something off one's chest' misleads toward confession.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid or suggestion put forward is a proposal.

indicators.note: no says the letter for shirt is taken out

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still waiting'
a T is a T-shirt, a kind of shirt

explanation.surface: Still not wearing a shirt on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes T (as in T-shirt) from STILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A window ledge is a narrow shelf at the base of a window frame.

parts.note: the phrase means achieving something difficult, and also literally tugging a label away

explanation.definitionFit: To achieve a tricky feat is to carry it through; literally it is tugging something away.

parts.note: the phrase is slang for getting started, but literally means became interwoven

explanation.definitionFit: Twisted or wound together, as strands are when interlaced.

clue.text: You will have to break one to make one

definitions.text: You will have to break one to make one

parts.words: You will have to break one to make one
parts.note: to set a new best performance you must exceed the existing best

explanation.definitionFit: A best-ever performance is set only by beating the previous best.
